## 1  picked-tube-name
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: scenario:declared-verification
says: When four colonies are picked into tubes, each tube is labelled with the construct name and a clone letter — pS-A, pS-B, pS-C, pS-D — and not a short code.
caption: Picking for Experiment declared-verification
  | label | clone | from plate
  | pS-A | Mach1/pS-A | Dpd
  | pS-B | Mach1/pS-B | Dpd
  | pS-C | Mach1/pS-C | Dpd
  | pS-D | Mach1/pS-D | Dpd

## 9  block-overflow
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: scenario:block-too-small
says: Thirty-two clones asked into one 24-well block is refused rather than seated somehow, and the message names the count and the vessel.
refused  session 6 (Picking) puts more than 24 clones in one 24-well block. Two blocks is a decision about the session, not about the layout — split the picking across two sittings, or say a larger `vessel=` on the line.

## 16  small-fragment-bind
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: scenario:short-product
says: A cleanup of a 231 bp fragment is told to bind with added isopropanol, because short DNA washes through a column under the standard bind.
caption: Gel, cleanup and assembly for Experiment short-product — on the page
  psfrag1 is under 250 bp, so the bind is 1 part ADB + 3 parts isopropanol — with ADB alone the fragment washes straight through and the tube comes off the column empty. The other tube is larger; the extra isopropanol costs them nothing, so the whole set is bound the same way.

## 17  three-plates

caption: Controls — three plates, the same for every kan transformation
  | plate | what goes on it | it answers
  | kan + | Mach1 + the kan control plasmid | the cells are competent and took up DNA
  | kan − | Mach1, no DNA added | the plate is not simply growing untransformed cells
  | kan streak | the kan control strain, streaked — not transformed | anything could have grown on this batch of kan plates

## 20  unknown-antibiotic
ruled: true, 2026-09-17
from: fault:unknown-antibiotic
says: A transformation that says to plate on something which is not the name of an antibiotic — "Bubba" where "Carb" belongs — is REFUSED. No workbook is written, and the message names the word it could not read and lists the ones it knows.
UNKNOWN_ANTIBIOTIC  step 2 says "Bubba" where an antibiotic belongs, and that is not a name this planner knows. It knows amp, ampicillin, cam, carb, carbenicillin, chlor, chloramphenicol, cm, erm, ery, erythromycin, kan, kanamycin, sp, spec, spectinomycin, tet, tetracycline. The file is refused: what to plate on decides whether the cells need an outgrowth before plating, and getting that wrong loses the whole plate silently.

## 21  no-antibiotic
ruled: true, 2026-09-17
from: fault:no-antibiotic
says: A transformation whose antibiotic cell is left EMPTY is refused as well. No workbook is written, and the message says the step does not say what to plate on and lists the names it will accept.
NO_ANTIBIOTIC  step 2 is a transformation that does not say what to plate on. The file is refused: whether the cells need an outgrowth before plating turns entirely on which antibiotic it is, so there is no safe default. Name one of amp, ampicillin, cam, carb, carbenicillin, chlor, chloramphenicol, cm, erm, ery, erythromycin, kan, kanamycin, sp, spec, spectinomycin, tet, tetracycline.

## 22  analysis-is-blank
ruled: true, 2026-09-17
from: scenario:minimal
says: The sequence analysis sheet arrives with its result and explanation columns EMPTY — one row per clone, for a person to fill in — and a fixed list of result tokens above it to choose from: Perfect, Perfect Partial, Silent Mutation, Missense Mutation and the rest.
caption: Result tokens — use one of these exactly
  | token | what it means
  | Perfect | Full region covered, matches the model.
  | Perfect Partial | Matches where readable, but the region is not fully covered.
  | Silent Mutation | Base change in the ORF, same amino acid.
  | Missense Mutation | Base change in the ORF, the amino acid changes.
  | Nonsense Mutation | Base change in the ORF, creates a stop codon.
  | Indel | Insertion or deletion in the region — may frameshift.
  | Mixed Clone | Two sequences in one trace; the colony was not clonal.
  | Failed | Read unusable, or it will not align to the target.

## 36  stock-sheet-is-prose
ruled: true, 2026-09-17
from: scenario:minimal
says: The antibiotic stock session has NO table at all — no rows, no columns. It is three notes: that the inventory records no kan stock, to check the shelf before weighing anything, and that plates and media are made from this so it comes first.
caption: Antibiotic stocks for Experiment minimal — notes on the page
  The inventory does not record a stock of kan. Check the shelf before you weigh anything — if there is one, write down where you found it and skip this session.
  Plates and media are made from this stock, so it comes before everything else.
  Tube labels start "My", taken from the folder name. Not checked against other experiments in the lab — nothing here can see them.

## 37  method-not-described
ruled: true, 2026-09-17
from: fault:method-not-described
says: A characterization step asking to electroporate into an organism this toolkit has no procedure for is REFUSED. No workbook is written. The message names the organism, says a protocol is per ORGANISM rather than per method, and says where to add one.
METHOD_NOT_DESCRIBED  step 1 asks for an electroporation into B.subtilis, and this toolkit has no procedure for that. A protocol is per ORGANISM, not per method — the voltage, the recovery medium and the temperatures are properties of the cells, so the nearest other one would be wrong rather than approximate. Nothing was written. Describe how B.subtilis is done and add it to `design/retransform.js § PROTOCOLS`, then compile again.

## 38  lactis-has-its-own-numbers
ruled: true, 2026-09-17
from: scenario:four-constructs
says: Name L.lactis instead and the same file compiles, and the protocol underneath carries the ORGANISM’S numbers rather than the file’s: a 0.2 cm cuvette at 2.0 kV, 40 µL of cells, 1 µL of DNA, 1 mL of recovery medium, 30 °C. The file says none of those and is not asked to.
caption: what the protocol carries, because it is the organism’s and not the file’s
  |  | 
  | cuvette | 0.2 cm
  | pulse | 2.0 kV — 10 kV/cm
  | time constant to expect | 5 ms
  | cells / DNA per reaction | 40 µL / 1 µL
  | recovery | 1000 µL, 60–120 min at 30 °C
  | harvested at | OD600 0.2–0.3
  | plated | 10, 100, 900 µL

## 39  refuse-duplicate
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:duplicate-product
says: Two steps that both claim to make `frag` is refused, and the message names `frag`.
DUPLICATE_PRODUCT  "frag" is produced twice in one file
DUPLICATE_PRODUCT  "frag" is produced twice — at step 1 and step 2. Later references are ambiguous.

## 40  refuse-no-product
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:no-product
says: A characterization line naming no product is refused, and the message names the line number and says a step needs both a subject and a product.
NO_PRODUCT  line 1 names 1 unnamed value(s); a step needs both a subject and a product so later steps can refer to it.

## 41  refuse-cycle
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:cycle
says: Two steps that each wait for the other are refused as a cycle rather than being put in some order anyway.
CYCLE  "a" is needed to make itself — following its inputs leads back to it, through b. There is no order these steps can be done in, so none of them was planned.
CYCLE  "b" is needed to make itself — following its inputs leads back to it, through a. There is no order these steps can be done in, so none of them was planned.
USE_BEFORE_PRODUCED  step 1 uses "b", which step 2 produces. Steps run in order.

## 42  unknown-verb
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:unknown-operation
says: A verb the grammar does not know is named, the message lists the verbs that ARE known, and no labsheets are written.
DUPLICATE_PRODUCT  "frag" is produced twice in one file
DUPLICATE_PRODUCT  (read generically: C6 could not parse this file, so inputs and outputs were taken as "first token is the operation, last is the product, the rest are inputs". Treat as a lead, not a verdict.) "frag" is produced twice — at step 1 and step 2. Later references are ambiguous.
UNKNOWN_OPERATION  "Frobnicate" is not an operation this planner knows
UNKNOWN_OPERATION  line 1 of pOK begins with "Frobnicate", which C6 does not know. Known operations: pcr, digest, ligate, gibson, goldengate, transform. THIS IS A TOOLCHAIN GAP, NOT NECESSARILY A BROKEN FILE — the parser treats an unknown verb as sequence data, which is why it complains about sequence format. The file may be perfectly good and unreadable by C6.

## 43  missing-clone-base
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:cannot-expand
says: A miniprep over a picked block with no clone= is reported once, naming the one word that would fix it — not once per clone.
CANNOT_EXPAND  miniprep pOK_dna: this step renames the clones above it and has no clone= to rename them to, so its 4 product(s) would keep the names Mach1/pOK-A … and collide with them. Add clone=<new base> to the line — a miniprep of a picked colony is a different tube from the colony.

## 44  long-name-warns
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:long-name
says: A construct name too long for a tube cap is a WARNING and the experiment still compiles, because the name came from the file and that is the author’s to choose.
LONG_NAME  the file's product is "pVeryLongConstructName", which is 22 characters. That name goes on a 1.5 mL cap with a clone designation after it — "pVeryLongConstructName-A" — and on the sequencing tube after that. 6 or fewer is the aim and 8 is about the limit of what somebody will write by hand. Longer is writeable and less legible, and this is the moment to think about it: after the file is written the name is the key every later step resolves through.

## 45  session-order
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: scenario:phase-two
says: The sessions come out in an order somebody could actually work: stocks and dilutions first, then PCR, then the gel and assembly, then the transformation, and the sequence analysis before anything that uses a verified plasmid.
caption: the sessions, in order
  | # | session | operations
  | 1 | Antibiotic stocks | stock
  | 2 | Oligo dilutions | dilution
  | 3 | PCR | pcr
  | 4 | Gel, cleanup and assembly | gel + zymo + goldengate
  | 5 | Transformation | transform
  | 6 | Picking | pick
  | 7 | Miniprep and sequencing | miniprep + sequencing
  | 8 | Sequence analysis | analysis
  | 9 | Electroporation | retransform
  | 10 | Picking and inoculation | pick + culture
  | 11 | Assay | assay

## 47  silent-use-before
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:use-before-produced
says: A construction file that says `GoldenGate frag1 …` on line 1 and `PCR … frag1` on line 2 — consuming a fragment the NEXT line makes — is now refused, naming both lines.
USE_BEFORE_PRODUCED  step 1 uses "bb", which step 3 produces. Steps run in order.
USE_BEFORE_PRODUCED  step 1 uses "frag", which step 2 produces. Steps run in order.

## 48  silent-bad-inventory
ruled: true, 2026-09-15
from: fault:inventory-unreadable
says: An inventory file that is prose rather than a freezer produces no message either — it reads as an EMPTY freezer, which is a different thing.
INVENTORY_UNREADABLE  the inventory is empty or could not be read — refusing to report every oligo as needing to be ordered
